provenance.author: block writer B6 (Claude Opus 5.5, model-written)
notes: Continuity audit 2026-10-18 applied: s126 no longer puts the wool beard in Mali's sack (in 36 it is in Cai's).

Codex review 2026-10-18 applied: the real/unreal labels are gone (rule_cy, s008 gloss, table caption, nodyn_en, pattern card, SVG): os = open condition ('efallai'), taswn = hypothetical ('syniad yn y pen'); C2 accepts 'O wlân du a gwlân gwyn'; B1 'mae hi'n deall pethau'n gyflym'. s074 calque 'Rhoddodd Elen y tân mas': its suggested diffodd is new vocabulary, so it is rephrased with known taro ('Tarodd Elen y tân bach gyda'i llaw') instead. Verdicts recorded.

Length about 1,530 words against 1,720 (window from 1,548): the council has six plans and a decision; adding more plans would be padding. The one lint-a-ac hit ('a oedd') is the interrogative particle in a reported question.

Target G34 core: taswn i / baswn i and tasai / basai (with faswn i ddim, fasai fe), about 30 times; every plan in the council is a conditional (Cai's fight, Cynyr's beard, Arthur's fake beard, Modlen's wool beard, Dafi's smoke beard, Myrddin's line about kings and wizards, Arthur's decision). Contrast with real os + bydd/present: Cai's 'Os bydd angen brenin barfog …', Mali's 'os ydy e'n falch' and 'Os bydd angen'. Other persons (baset ti, basen ni, basech chi, basen nhw) are not used; pe bai occurs once in Mali's mouth ('like a book', Cai teases her) and is glossed '= tasai (llyfr)'.

Promotion point honoured: llai (llai trwm), gwaeth (Basai hynny'n waeth na'r cawr! / mêl … yn waeth na chawr) and gwaethaf (Dyna'r cynllun gwaethaf!) are used productively; Gramadeg adds a gwell / gwaeth / llai table.
No deliberate Dafi error in this chapter (he speaks correct conditionals).
No open-slot words. Forms added to cy-gofyn: gofynnais i, gofynnaist ti (not derivable by the -ais suffix rule because of the double n).
SVG cy-brenin-01-l34-img-os-taswn.svg authored (Welsh labels; viewBox 300 wide, 17px text).

Continuity: sets up 36–37 as written by the 37 writer: Arthur decides they go to Eryri together, without an army and without sending a beard (Cai, Mali, Dafi, Pero, and Myrddin 'os ydy e eisiau'); Cynyr stays in Caerllion (Arthur's joke about the most bearded lord); Modlen stays ('Faswn i ddim yn mynd i ben mynydd …') but will pack food. The wool beard goes too, and Cai claims it: 'Os bydd angen brenin barfog, fi fydd y brenin barfog!' (he wears it on the summit in 37). Myrddin: 'Dim hud heddiw … Mae ffrindiau gyda ti. Mae hynny'n well na hud' (37: 'Heddiw, does dim hud'). Modlen's question in 33 (does the giant see well?) is explained: a wool beard might pass at a distance. Mali packs needle, thread and scissors. Dafi's smoke beard and accidental flame foreshadow the blinding smoke of 37.

Recall pass 2026-10-18: recurrences for Penodau 29–33 vocabulary in the council (bygythiad, erbyn, gorchfygu, heddwch, neu, gwrthod, anrhydedd, llythyr, gorffen, urddas, profi, nerfus, esgob, swyddogol, gwisg, tyst, brifo, ysbryd, rhybuddio, gelyn, dadl, anghydfod, ffermwr, barnu, dibynnu, ymddiried, arweinydd, gobaith, trefnu). Voice fix: s018 'Gwenodd Cynyr, ond' → 'ac'. New segments s301–s309, s311–s312 (s310 drafted and withdrawn in the same pass; not to be reused).

Recall pass, pruning 2026-10-18 (docs/reviews/recall-pass-critique-2026-10-18.md): applied the critique's revert/rework rows (s305, s062, s066, s309, s311, s312). Deleted new segments' IDs are retired, not to be reused; some recall targets deliberately left unmet rather than re-placed.

review_questions.resolution: Codex: keep a thasai (a + AM) as the written model.

review_questions.question: [?] Negative protasis 'Tasai'r cawr ddim yn gweld yn dda' (colloquial) vs 'Tasai'r cawr ddim yn gallu gweld': natural?

[?] 'arogli o ddefaid / o fêl' (smell of sheep / of honey): natural?

primary_new_grammar.label: Conditional core: taswn i … baswn i … / tasai fe … basai fe … for imagined plans; faswn i ddim / fasai fe ddim; contrast with the open condition os + present/future (Pennod 21). pe bai (Mali, 'like a book') and fasech chi / other persons are receptive only. llai and gwaeth / gwaethaf used productively (promotion point).

cover.alt: A council of friends around a table in a small room of the castle: Arthur wears a huge black-and-white wool beard stuck on with honey while Pero sniffs it, and everyone laughs except Modlen.
cover.art_brief: A small timber-and-brick room off the great hall at Caerllion, morning light from one small window (Caerllion palette). Around a wooden table: Arthur (12, untidy brown hair with a cowlick, freckles; plain blue cloak over a long blue robe with a small red dragon on the chest) (no crown) sits wearing an enormous fake beard of black and white wool, honey dripping at its edges, cross-eyed as Pero (large shaggy black-and-white hound, grey muzzle) stands with his front paws on the bench and pushes his wet nose into the woolly beard. Modlen (short, round, rosy, white headscarf, long floury apron, big wooden spoon) stands proudly beside him with a pot of honey and her spoon, frowning at Pero. Cai (15, tall, red-blond, rust-red tunic, red cloak, sword at his belt) roars with laughter; Mali (12, long dark braid, dark-blue dress, satchel) laughs into her hand, a needle, thread and scissors on the table in front of her; Cynyr (broad, huge golden-blond beard to mid-chest, brown cloak with round silver brooch) (one side of his golden beard cut short) and Elen (about fifty, white linen veil, forest-green dress, ring of keys) smile. Dafi (cup-sized red dragon, two short cream horns, tiny bat wings, big yellow eyes; small enough to sit in a wooden drinking cup) peeps from the tall black hat of Myrddin (very old, thin, long white beard, round wire spectacles, patched deep-blue robe, tall black brimmed hat), who stands by the window. No text.

segments.text: Yn y bore, roedd y ffrindiau'n eistedd wrth y bwrdd yn yr ystafell fach wrth y neuadd: Arthur, Cai, Mali, Cynyr ac Elen.
Roedd Pero'n cysgu dan y bwrdd, ac roedd Myrddin wrth y ffenest gyda'i het.
"Mae angen cynllun arnon ni," meddai Arthur.
segments.speaker: char-arth

segments.text: "Dewch: dyn ni'n trafod bygythiad y cawr heddiw."
"Rhaid i ni gael cynllun erbyn y lleuad newydd.
Oes syniad gyda chi?"
"Oes!" meddai Cai, a chododd e ei gleddyf.
segments.speaker: char-cai

segments.text: "Taswn i'n frenin, baswn i'n ymladd.

inference_aids.gloss: taswn … baswn …: syniad yn y pen

segments.text: Baswn i'n mynd i Eryri, baswn i'n taro'r cawr ar ei drwyn, a baswn i'n ei orchfygu e!"
"Ond dwyt ti ddim yn frenin, Cai," meddai Mali.
segments.speaker: char-mali

segments.text: "A thasai Cai'n mynd i Eryri gyda'i gleddyf, basai'r cawr yn ei fwyta e i frecwast."
"Faswn i ddim yn cwympo," meddai Cai. "Dw i'n gryf!"
segments.speaker: char-cai

segments.text: "Mae'r cawr yn gryfach," meddai Mali. "Dyna syniad twp."
segments.speaker: char-mali

segments.text: Wedyn cododd Cynyr. Rhoddodd e ei law ar ei farf, a dwedodd e:
"Taswn i'n eillio fy marf i, a'i hanfon hi at Rhita, basai'r cawr yn hapus. Mae hi'n hir ar un ochr eto!"
segments.speaker: char-cynyr

segments.text: "Barf neu heddwch? Heddwch, wrth gwrs!"
"Basai'r cawr yn gwybod," meddai Elen yn dawel. "Dyw e ddim eisiau barf arglwydd: mae e eisiau barf brenin."
segments.speaker: char-elen

segments.text: "A Dad," meddai Arthur, "taswn i'n cymryd dy farf di, faswn i ddim yn frenin da."
segments.speaker: char-arth

segments.text: "Dw i'n gwrthod dy farf di, Dad: dy anrhydedd di yw hi."
Gwenodd Cynyr, ac roedd e'n falch. "Rwyt ti'n ddewr, fy mab," meddai e.
"Taswn i'n anfon llythyr at Rhita, basai fe'n darllen am heddwch," meddai Mali.
segments.speaker: char-mali

segments.text: "Dyw cawr ddim yn darllen llythyr, Mali," meddai Cai.
segments.speaker: char-cai

segments.text: "Mae syniad gyda fi hefyd, ond dyw e ddim yn dda," meddai Arthur. "Taswn i'n anfon barf ffug, basai'r cawr yn gwybod."
segments.speaker: char-arth

segments.text: Yn sydyn, agorodd y drws, a daeth Modlen i'r ystafell gyda basged fawr.
"Barf ffug?" meddai Modlen. "Pwy sy'n siarad am farf ffug? Fi sy wedi gwneud un!"
segments.speaker: char-modlen

segments.text: Agorodd Modlen y fasged, a chododd hi farf fawr, hir. Roedd hi'n ddu ac yn wyn, ac roedd hi'n hir iawn.
"Dyma hi!" meddai Modlen. "Barf ffug, o'r gwlân du a'r gwlân gwyn o'r ffair.
segments.speaker: char-modlen

segments.text: Ces i nodwydd ac edau gan Elen, a siswrn gan y morynion, a gweithiais i drwy'r nos."

inference_aids.art_brief: A sewing set laid out side by side: a long steel needle, a small reel of thread, and a pair of old iron scissors, beside a tuft of black-and-white wool. Ink line and watercolour, transparent background, no text.

segments.text: Edrychodd pawb ar y farf. Roedd hi'n fawr iawn, yn fwy na barf Cynyr.
"Gwaith da, Modlen," meddai Elen. "Mae hi'n edrych yn dda iawn."
segments.speaker: char-elen

segments.text: "Syniad clyfar, Modlen," meddai Arthur.
segments.speaker: char-arth

segments.text: "Wrth gwrs," meddai Modlen. "Nawr, Arthur: eistedd. Rhaid i fi ei gludo hi ar dy wyneb di."
segments.speaker: char-modlen

segments.text: "Ei gludo hi? Gyda beth?"
segments.speaker: char-arth

segments.text: "Gyda mêl, wrth gwrs. Does dim esgus: eistedd!"
segments.speaker: char-modlen

segments.text: Eisteddodd Arthur, a rhoddodd Modlen fêl ar ei wyneb e.
Wedyn gludodd hi'r farf wlân ar y mêl.
Penderfynodd Arthur fod mêl ar ei wyneb yn waeth na chawr.
"Ha!" meddai Cai. "Brenin barfog! Mae Arthur yn hen ddyn nawr! Ble mae dy urddas di, frenin?"
segments.speaker: char-cai

segments.text: Ond yn sydyn, cododd Pero o dan y bwrdd.
Roedd e'n arogli'r farf a'r mêl.
Wedyn rhoddodd e ei drwyn mawr, gwlyb ar wyneb y brenin!
"Mae Pero'n meddwl dy fod di'n ddafad, Arthur!" meddai Mali. "Mae'r farf yn arogli o ddefaid, ac o fêl."
segments.speaker: char-mali

segments.text: Roedd pawb yn chwerthin, ond doedd Modlen ddim yn chwerthin.
"Pero! Paid!" meddai hi. "Mae'r farf yn ddoniol, ydy, ond mae hi'n farf dda!"
segments.speaker: char-modlen

segments.text: "Mae hi'n ddoniol iawn," meddai Mali.
segments.speaker: char-mali

segments.text: "Rhy ddoniol. Taswn i'n gawr, baswn i'n chwerthin hefyd.
A thasai'r cawr yn gweld y farf hon yn agos, basai fe'n gwybod: barf ffug yw hi."
"Yn agos, ie," meddai Modlen.
segments.speaker: char-modlen

segments.text: "Ond yn bell? Gofynnais i ddoe a oedd y cawr yn gweld yn dda, a does neb yn gwybod."
"Dyna pam gofynnaist ti!" meddai Mali. "Rwyt ti'n glyfar, Modlen."
segments.speaker: char-mali

segments.text: "Wrth gwrs," meddai Modlen eto.
segments.speaker: char-modlen

segments.text: "Fi yw'r gogyddes. Nawr, rhaid i ni brofi bod y farf yn gweithio!
Cer i'r neuadd fawr yn y farf, Arthur, a phaid â siarad.
Tasai pawb yn gwybod, basai pawb yn chwerthin."
Aeth Arthur i'r neuadd fawr yn ei wisg las, gyda'r farf wlân ar ei wyneb, ac roedd e'n nerfus. Roedd Mali a Cai'n gwylio o'r drws.
Yn gyntaf, daeth morwyn gyda llestri. Edrychodd hi ar y dyn barfog, a cherddodd hi heibio i Arthur heb ddweud dim byd.
Wedyn daeth Barf Goch. Edrychodd e ar y farf hir, ddu a gwyn, ac edrychodd e eto.
"Bore da, hen ddewin," meddai e, a cherddodd e mas o'r neuadd.
segments.speaker: char-barf-goch

inference_aids.alt: The beard test in the great hall: Arthur in a huge black-and-white wool beard stands still while Barf Goch, the red-bearded lord, looks twice at him from a few paces away and greets him as an old wizard; Cai and Mali giggle in the doorway.
inference_aids.art_brief: The great hall of the castle at Caerllion by day, long tables cleared. In the middle stands Arthur (12, untidy brown hair with a cowlick, freckles; plain blue cloak over a long blue robe with a small red dragon on the chest) (no crown) wearing an enormous fake beard of black-and-white wool down to his belt, keeping very still and solemn; his small boots show under the robe. A few paces away (the beard only works from afar, s055), the big lord with a bushy red beard (Barf Goch) in a fur-trimmed black cloak looks at the beard a second time, puzzled, half bowing, as if greeting an old wizard (s053-s054). A maid with a stack of dishes glances at the bearded figure and walks past without a word (s052). In a doorway Cai (15, tall, red-blond, rust-red tunic, red cloak, sword at his belt) and Mali (12, long dark braid, dark-blue dress, satchel) clutch each other trying not to laugh (s051). (Myrddin comes in only at s056, so he is not shown.) No text.

segments.speaker: char-cai

segments.text: Yn olaf, daeth Myrddin i'r neuadd. Edrychodd e ar y dyn barfog am funud, a gwenodd e.

segments.speaker: char-myrddin

segments.text: "Sut dych chi'n gwybod?"
segments.speaker: char-arth

segments.text: "Mae dy draed di'n rhy fach i hen ddewin," meddai Myrddin.
segments.speaker: char-myrddin

segments.text: "Tasai'r cawr yn edrych ar dy draed di, basai fe'n gwybod hefyd.

segments.speaker: char-mali

segments.text: Wedyn daeth pen bach coch o het Myrddin.
"Mae syniad gyda fi!" meddai Dafi.
segments.speaker: char-dafi

segments.text: "Barf o fwg! Taswn i'n tisian ar wyneb Arthur, basai barf o fwg gyda fe: barf fawr, lwyd, heb fêl!"

segments.speaker: char-arth

segments.text: Hedfanodd Dafi at wyneb Arthur, a thisianodd e: "A… a… atishŵ!"
Am funud, roedd barf fawr, lwyd ar wyneb y brenin: barf o fwg. Roedd hi'n wych.

inference_aids.alt: Dafi sneezes a beard of grey smoke onto Arthur's face; for a moment the boy-king has a great grey beard, and Mali is opening the window.
inference_aids.art_brief: The same small room at Caerllion. Arthur (12, untidy brown hair with a cowlick, freckles; plain blue cloak over a long blue robe with a small red dragon on the chest) sits very still with his eyes closed while Dafi (cup-sized red dragon, two short cream horns, tiny bat wings, big yellow eyes; small enough to sit in a wooden drinking cup), hovering on tiny wings at his chin, sneezes a cloud of grey smoke that hangs on his face in the shape of a long, curly grey beard. On the table, the black-and-white wool beard lies beside a honey pot. Modlen (short, round, rosy, white headscarf, long floury apron, big wooden spoon) has her spoon raised in alarm. No text.

segments.text: "Aros di yng Nghaerllion, Dad," meddai Arthur. "Taswn i'n mynd gyda'r arglwydd mwyaf barfog yng Nghymru, basai'r cawr yn hapus iawn!"
segments.speaker: char-arth

segments.text: Roedd Cynyr yn chwerthin yn uchel, ac roedd pawb yn chwerthin gydag e.
"A fi?" meddai Modlen. "Faswn i ddim yn mynd i ben mynydd am bob pastai yng Nghymru.
segments.speaker: char-modlen

segments.text: Ond bydda i'n trefnu bwyd i'r daith!"
"Dyna esgus da," meddai Cai.
segments.speaker: char-cai

segments.text: "Dyw e ddim yn esgus, Cai," meddai Modlen. "Mae e'n wir! Bara, caws, cig a mêl, a dim pasteiod i'r ddraig!"
segments.speaker: char-modlen

segments.text: "Dim pasteiod?" meddai Dafi o'r het. "Taswn i'n gawr, baswn i'n bwyta pob pastai yng Nghaerllion!"
segments.speaker: char-dafi

segments.text: "Gyda'n gilydd, felly!" meddai Cai, a chododd e ei gleddyf a'r farf wlân. "Cawr, dyma ni!"
segments.speaker: char-cai

segments.text: Y noson honno, rhoddodd Mali'r nodwydd, yr edau a'r siswrn yn ei sach.
"Os bydd angen," meddai hi.
segments.speaker: char-mali

grammar.nodyn_en: Hypothetical conditions: taswn i (if I were / did) … baswn i (I would) …; tasai … basai … for he, she or a noun. Negatives and questions soft-mutate: Faswn i ddim, Fasai fe …? Open conditions keep os + present or future (Pennod 21). Pe bai is the book form of tasai; other persons come in Pennod 37.
